about: What each measured CONFIGURATION is, and the controls a run of it must show in the same invocation before a silence counts as MISSED (tools/verdicts.py). An arm NAME in a case.json is a label; a corpus maps each of its arm names to one configuration here (corpus.json `arm_configurations`), so two corpora whose `spatial` means different things cannot be added up as if it did not. A control's expectation is part of the configuration's identity: a use-after-free control that COMPLETES is what shows an arm does not revoke, just as one that faults shows it does.

app-level0.summary: an application domain on a physical-profile SDK, whose heap is level0: malloc bounds each object to its request; free revokes nothing; a nested allocator's chunks are unbounded inside the block it took

cheribsd-default.summary: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation at the platform default: malloc bounds each object; a freed object is quarantined and revoked by a later sweep
cheribsd-default.mechanism: per-object bounds in malloc; revocation after quarantine

virtual-mallocng.summary: the virtual Capstone profile (capstone/runtime/virtual, exact-bounds QEMU): the application runs as a Linux process under capstone-vexec with musl mallocng compiled for Capstone and run locally; malloc bounds each object exactly and free retires its lifetime, so a stale capability to it faults; a nested allocator's chunks are unbounded inside the block it took. Not the physical Sublet heap: its own lifetime mechanism (runtime/virtual/mallocng.md)
virtual-mallocng.mechanism: per-object exact bounds and lifetime retirement in malloc

virtual-mallocng-pg-pools.summary: virtual-mallocng plus the memory-context port's patch 0003 in the server, built for the virtual profile (ports/common/application/build-virtual.sh postgres with PGSU_NESTED=sublet): every palloc chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), bounded to the request and revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE)
virtual-mallocng-pg-pools.mechanism: as virtual-mallocng; per-chunk bounds and revocation in palloc

virtual-mallocng-replay.summary: the memory-contexts replay built as a Capstone application (capstone-application toolchain, virtual SDK) and run as a process under capstone-vexec: PostgreSQL's managers with the capability-layout patches on virtual mallocng, which bounds and retires each block it hands the manager but not the chunks carved from it
virtual-mallocng-replay.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of malloc blocks; none per chunk

virtual-mallocng-replay-pools.summary: the same replay with PG_SUBLET, which applies the port's patch 0003: every chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), bounded to the request and revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE)
virtual-mallocng-replay-pools.mechanism: as virtual-mallocng-replay; per-chunk bounds and revocation in the memory contexts

virtual-sqlite-memsys5.summary: SQLite 3.22.0 built for the virtual profile with memsys5 stock over one static array (ports/sqlite/repro322/build-virtual.py --memsys5): every SQLite allocation is an offset inside that arena, so the system allocator -- virtual mallocng -- sees one object and no frees

virtual-sqlite-memsys5-pools.summary: the same static arena with memsys5 on its Sublet port (build-virtual.py --sublet, ports/sqlite/sublet/sublet-3220000-memsys5.patch): every block goes out as a child lifetime of the pool (CDERIVE), bounded to its request rounded to 8 bytes, and sqlite3_free revokes it (CREVOKE); the lookaside's slots the same, revoked by sqlite3DbFree. The page cache is not covered
virtual-sqlite-memsys5-pools.mechanism: per-block bounds and revocation in memsys5 (CDERIVE/CREVOKE)

virtual-pymalloc.summary: CPython 3.13.7's obmalloc as the pymalloc replay (ports/cpython/pymalloc, capstone-application preset, virtual SDK) run as a process under capstone-vexec: pymalloc stock, its arena one aligned_alloc block from virtual mallocng, every pymalloc block an unbounded offset inside it
virtual-pymalloc.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of the arena only; none per pymalloc block

virtual-pymalloc-pools.summary: the same replay built with PYMALLOC_SUBLET, which applies the port's patch 0003: obmalloc hands out every block as a child lifetime of its arena, bounded to the request (CDERIVE), and revokes it on free (CREVOKE)
virtual-pymalloc-pools.mechanism: as virtual-pymalloc; per-block bounds and revocation inside obmalloc

virtual-ffmpeg-carve.summary: FFmpeg's carved corpus on virtual mallocng (-DFFC_SUBLET_CARVE): each disjoint region is a bounded CDERIVE child of the block; CREVOKE ends a region and free ends every descendant
virtual-ffmpeg-carve.mechanism: per-region bounds and revocation in the carve port, over virtual mallocng

virtual-memcached-stock.summary: memcached/allocator-repros on the virtual profile with slabs.c/cache.c STOCK on virtual mallocng: the allocators port's hosted build with the stock ledger (-DMCP_STOCK_MALLOC=ON, as the ASan arm), built by the corpus's shared/build-cases.sh capstone-application, so every slab page and every cache.c object is one virtual-mallocng object -- a chunk carries its page's bound, an object its own, and nothing is retired until a page or object is given back
virtual-memcached-stock.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of every page and object the allocators take from the system; none per chunk, none on a free-list transition

virtual-memcached-ledger.summary: the same corpus on the port's shared ledger over the Sublet authority in the process (-DMCP_SUBLET=ON, shared/driver-virtual.c): the payload is lent by the virtual heap as one linear capability (capstone_borrow_aligned_block), every chunk and object a lease bounded to itself, revoked when slabs.c or cache.c takes it back (mode 1); with the carve remedy (MC_CARVE_BOUNDS) for 06 and 07, as the physical column 3 reads sublet-carve for them. SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11 by virtual-memcached-sublet: the ledger's Sublet authority and the lent payload were removed with the lend API; kept to judge the 2026-10-10 bundle
virtual-memcached-ledger.mechanism: per-chunk and per-object bounds and revocation in the allocators, over a payload the virtual heap lends; for 06 and 07 also the item's key/suffix carve

virtual-memcached-sublet.summary: the same corpus with the application's Sublet patch 0006 in slabs.c and cache.c (the allocators port's -DMCP_SUBLET=ON, shared/driver-virtual.c, `fixed|buggy N`): no hooks and no ledger; pages and objects come from virtual mallocng as upstream's come from malloc, every chunk and object is a CDERIVE child of its page's generation or of the object's lifetime, bounded to the chunk or object, and slabs_free/cache_free revoke it (CREVOKE); with the carve remedy (MC_CARVE_BOUNDS) for 06 and 07, as the physical column 3 read sublet-carve for them
virtual-memcached-sublet.mechanism: per-chunk and per-object bounds and revocation by the allocators' own two lifetime instructions; for 06 and 07 also the item's key/suffix carve

virtual-wmem.summary: Wireshark's wmem (core and its four allocators, 4.6.8) with the corpus driver's scope model, built as a Capstone application (ports/wireshark/wmem, capstone-application preset, virtual SDK) and run as a process under capstone-vexec: wmem as released, its g_malloc virtual mallocng, which bounds and retires each block and jumbo it hands wmem but not the objects block and block_fast carve from a block
virtual-wmem.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of malloc blocks; none per wmem object

virtual-wmem-pools.summary: the same with WM_SUBLET, which applies the port's patch 0001: every object of the block and block_fast allocators a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), bounded to the request, revoked by free, realloc and the reset that ends its pool (CREVOKE)
virtual-wmem-pools.mechanism: as virtual-wmem; per-object bounds and revocation inside block and block_fast

virtual-cpython.summary: the CPython 3.13.7 interpreter for the virtual profile (ports/common/application/build-virtual.sh cpython, CPY_TEST_CAPI=1) run as a process under capstone-vexec: its one heap is musl mallocng, which bounds and retires every object it hands out -- PyMem_Raw allocations, objects over 512 bytes, and the arenas pymalloc takes -- while pymalloc stock (patch 0009) carves its blocks inside those arenas unbounded
virtual-cpython.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of malloc objects; none per pymalloc block

virtual-cpython-pools.summary: the same interpreter built with CPY_SUBLET=1: patch 0014 makes obmalloc hand out every block as a child lifetime of its arena, bounded to the request (CDERIVE), and revoke it on free (CREVOKE); the arena's own child dies with the arena when mallocng frees it; requests over 512 bytes go to mallocng, as in the stock arm
virtual-cpython-pools.mechanism: as virtual-cpython; per-block bounds and revocation inside obmalloc

virtual-ffmpeg-pool-stock.summary: ffmpeg/pool-repros on the virtual profile with AVBufferPool and AVRefStructPool STOCK: the buffer-pool port's capstone-application library (patch 0001 only), its av_malloc the process's malloc, built by the corpus's shared/build-cases.sh, so every pool entry is one virtual-mallocng object, bounded and never freed while the pool lives; a buffer returned to the pool is retired by nothing
virtual-ffmpeg-pool-stock.mechanism: exact bounds and lifetime retirement of every entry and object the pools take from the system; none on a return to the pool

virtual-ffmpeg-pool-sublet.summary: the same corpus with -DFFPOOL_SUBLET=ON, which applies the port's patch 0003: every buffer or refstruct object a pool hands out is a child lifetime of its entry (CDERIVE), bounded to it and revoked when it returns to the pool (CREVOKE)
virtual-ffmpeg-pool-sublet.mechanism: per-hand-out bounds and revocation in AVBufferPool and AVRefStructPool

silicon-level0-lifetimes.summary: the case built for the silicon ABI (runtime/silicon/build-b0-hello.sh: gp-captable, full LTO, soft float, the pool carve) and run on the FPGA as a delegated application through capstone-exec, its heap level0 built with CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_LIFETIMES: every object is a CDERIVE child of one MANAGE group over the arena, at exactly its request size on a 16-byte placement, and free CREVOKEs it, so a stale capability's next use traps 25; inexact requests keep plain bounds and no lifetime. First measured on caplifive_sublet_d93a8d66b (silicon-runs/2026-10-16-plain); since dev 2c53d5641b72 free finds the block by address and revokes the child recorded in its header (the plain corpora's 2026-10-16 bundles ran the earlier free, and read the same on QEMU after it)
silicon-level0-lifetimes.mechanism: per-object exact bounds and a CDERIVE/CREVOKE lifetime per object in level0, on silicon

silicon-level0.summary: the same silicon-ABI build and board run as silicon-level0-lifetimes with level0 as it ships: malloc bounds each object to its request (SHRINK) and free only marks the block free, so a temporal case completes by construction; the bounds-only control arm
silicon-level0.mechanism: per-object bounds in level0, on silicon

silicon-level0-subobject.summary: silicon-level0 with every case, driver and pool source and the controls compiled with -Xclang -fcapstone-subobject-bounds: a pointer to a struct member is bounded to that member, so a crossing that stays inside one allocation can fault; level0 revokes nothing
silicon-level0-subobject.mechanism: struct-field bounds from the compiler over level0's per-object bounds, on silicon

silicon-ffmpeg-pool-stock.summary: FFmpeg's pool-repros on silicon over the silicon-level0-lifetimes heap, its AVBufferPool stock with the port's event tracing (patch 0001): a buffer returned to the pool stays reachable through a stale pointer, so pool control 90 completes
silicon-ffmpeg-pool-stock.mechanism: per-object lifetimes in malloc; the nested pool stock

silicon-ffmpeg-pool-sublet.summary: the same over the silicon-level0-lifetimes heap with the protected pools (patch 0003): every pooled buffer is a CDERIVE child of its pool entry, CREVOKEd when it returns to the pool, so pool control 90 faults with cause 25 at read_probe
silicon-ffmpeg-pool-sublet.mechanism: per-object lifetimes in malloc and a lifetime per pooled buffer

silicon-ffmpeg-carve-level0.summary: FFmpeg's carved-repros on silicon over level0 as it ships, with no carve narrowing: a crossing that stays inside the carved block is invisible to the block's own bound. The carve control (shared/carve-control.c, case 99: one byte past a 16-byte carve inside its 64-byte block) completes
silicon-ffmpeg-carve-level0.mechanism: per-object bounds in level0; carves unbounded inside their block, on silicon

silicon-ffmpeg-carve-bounds.summary: the carved corpus built with -DFFC_CARVE_BOUNDS over level0: every carve is a capability narrowed to its region with SHRINK (__builtin_capstone_cap_shrink), so a crossing out of the region faults; bounds only, no lifetimes. The carve control faults
silicon-ffmpeg-carve-bounds.mechanism: SHRINK-narrowed carves over level0, on silicon

silicon-ffmpeg-carve-sublet.summary: the carved corpus built with -DFFC_SUBLET_CARVE over the silicon-level0-lifetimes heap: the driver CDERIVEs a group over each block and every carve is a CDERIVE child of that group, CREVOKEd on re-carve. The RTL rounds a CDERIVE child outward rather than refusing it, so a carve is not guaranteed exact (case 00's group is inexact). The carve control faults. The re-carve control (shared/carve-recarve-control.c, case 98) completes when the region is used live (live-carve) and faults when used after its re-carve (uaf-carve)
silicon-ffmpeg-carve-sublet.mechanism: a CDERIVE child per carve with CREVOKE on re-carve, over per-object lifetimes, on silicon
